$comment: The ice-height models, time scenarios and ocean basins of Martinec et al. (2018), tables 1, 2 and 3. All five cases use the same spherical cap shape as Spada et al. (2011) table 4 row 1, with an angular radius of 10 degrees, moved and rescaled.

source.citation: Martinec, Z. et al. (2018). Geophysical Journal International 215(1), 389-414, tables 1 to 4.

constants.$comment: The densities follow Spada et al. (2011). The surface gravity is the value the plotting scripts divide the gravitational potential by to obtain geoid height; it is the surface value of the M3-L70-V01 gravity profile, 9.815, carried to one more digit.

load_shape.name: Spherical cap, parabolic cross-section
load_shape.surface_mass_density: sigma_ice(Omega, t) = rho_ice * h_ice(Omega, t), with the cap profile of Spada et al. (2011) table 4 row 1

L0.note: The model used in Spada et al. (2011).

L1.note: Thick enough that the ice never floats when it meets the ocean.

L2.note: Low enough that the condition for floating ice is met when the cap reaches the coast, which is what cases C, D and E exercise.

T0.description: Heaviside loading. The height h(t) and the angular radius alpha(t) take their full values for t in (t0, t1].

T1.description: A linear increase of h(t) and alpha(t) from zero at t0 to their full values at t1, then held constant to t2.
T1.height: h(t0) = 0, h(t1) = h0, then h(t) = h0 for t in (t1, t2]
T1.radius: alpha(t0) = 0, alpha(t1) = alpha0, then alpha(t) = alpha0 for t in (t1, t2]

ocean_basins.$formula: zeta0(Omega) = bmax - b0 * exp(-psi^2 / (2 * sigma_b^2)), where cos(psi) = cos(theta)cos(theta_b) + sin(theta)sin(theta_b)cos(lambda - lambda_b). zeta0 is the solid Earth topography at the initial time. Its minimum is bmax - b0 at the basin centre and its maximum is bmax at the antipode.

B0.note: No ocean. The sea level equation is not solved.

B1.note: Far from the ice load, so the ice stays inland.

B2.note: Deep and close to the ice load, so a growing cap reaches the coast.

sea_level_equation_levels.1: Solved with a fixed ocean geometry.
sea_level_equation_levels.2: Solved with a time-varying ocean geometry, so the coastline moves and ice may float.

notes: The basin radius psi0 = sigma_b * sqrt(2 * ln(b0/bmax)) is 24.85 degrees for both B1 and B2, where zeta0 = 0. The paper prints the square root of ln(b0/bmax)^2 on p. 395, which gives 11.88 degrees; its figure 17 gives 24.8503 degrees, which only the form here reproduces.
Benchmark E uses basin B2*, which has the same parameters as B2 but prescribes the topography at the terminal time instead of the initial time, so the initial topography is the unknown.
